recognize_zh: 兩個子細胞各含一團緻密、分離的染色質，細胞質仍以狹窄橋樑相連、呈啞鈴形，是正在分裂末期（telophase）的細胞出現在周邊血液抹片中。
features: Dumbbell-shaped dividing cell with two daughter halves joined by a narrowing cytoplasmic bridge
Each half contains a dense, clumped chromatin mass without nuclear membrane or nucleolus
Moderate amount of basophilic blue cytoplasm
Nearby mononuclear cell with indented nucleus and blue cytoplasm (reactive lymphocyte or monocyte)
Background red cells with central pallor and scattered platelets; color cast of the photograph limits color assessment
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a cell in late mitosis (telophase), with two daughter cells each containing a condensed chromatin mass, separated by a narrowing cytoplasmic bridge with basophilic cytoplasm. A mononuclear cell with an indented nucleus and moderate blue cytoplasm is also present, while the red cells and platelets appear unremarkable. Mitotic figures are rarely seen in normal blood and may occur in reactive states with circulating immunoblasts, in marrow stress, or in leukemic and lymphoma circulation. Findings demonstrate a circulating telophase cell; the lineage cannot be determined morphologically and correlation with the full smear and CBC is advised.

ddx.dx: Binucleated cell (e.g., reactive lymphocyte or dyserythropoietic normoblast)
ddx.vs: Binucleate cells have two nuclei with intact nuclear membranes within one continuous cell rather than condensed chromosome masses at opposite poles.
Overlapping cells show separate complete cell borders, whereas telophase shows a single constricted cytoplasmic bridge.

ddx.dx: Circulating blasts or lymphoma cells in mitosis
ddx.vs: Neoplastic circulation would show additional blasts or atypical cells in the smear, which requires review beyond this field and flow cytometry.
